Global vs vegetation-specific s2biophys¶

Compare FAPAR and effective leaf area index (LAIe) retrieval maps for three small regions. Both models use the same Sentinel-2 observations, cloud mask, 20 m grid and temporal aggregation (predict each observation, then average). The global ensemble has five members; each independently optimized vegetation-specific ensemble has three.

The selected variant is applied to every valid pixel in the region, with no vegetation-class mask. These are model comparisons, not accuracy assessments against ground truth.

Run from this repository with gee-biophys, matplotlib and a Jupyter kernel installed. Authenticate once with earthengine authenticate; optionally set EE_PROJECT below. Downloads use xee and predictions run locally.

Setup and processing cells are collapsed; expand them to inspect or modify the workflow. Maps and summary tables remain visible.

Regions¶

The current configs use 5 km × 5 km squares in local UTM. They represent the requested vegetation settings but can contain mixed cover:

Region Variant Period Context
Lägeren, Switzerland temperate_broadleaf_forest June 2024 Beech-dominated forest (WSL)
Saguaro west, Arizona arid_shrubland August–September 2024 Low-elevation Sonoran desert scrub (USGS)
Konza Prairie, Kansas temperate_nonforest Mid Mai–Mid June 2024 Tallgrass prairie / agriculture (NEON)

The extents and dates come directly from the three tested example configs.

Sentinel-2 RGB and side-by-side retrievals¶

The first column is a true-colour B4/B3/B2 median composite of the same cloud-masked observations used for prediction. RGB uses a fixed 0–0.30 reflectance stretch and gamma 1.2 and a saturation factor of 1.5 across all regions. Gray RGB pixels have no valid observations.

All three columns share map bounds; the two retrieval columns share a color scale. Axes show distance in the local projected grid; north is up. Gray retrieval pixels have no paired valid retrieval. FAPAR/FCOVER are fractions; LAIe is m²/m².

FAPAR¶

Fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation; both models use the same 0–1 scale.

LAIe¶

Effective leaf area index (m²/m²); both models use the same 0–5 scale and the same input observations as FAPAR.

Numerical comparison¶

Differences are vegetation-specific minus global, computed over paired valid pixels separately for each trait.

trait region variant paired pixels global mean specific mean mean difference (specific − global) mean absolute difference
0 FAPAR Lägeren · broadleaf forest temperate_broadleaf_forest 62991 0.4872 0.5924 0.1052 0.1054
1 FAPAR Saguaro · arid shrubland arid_shrubland 63001 0.0377 0.0347 -0.0030 0.0081
2 FAPAR Konza prairie · grassland temperate_nonforest 63001 0.4535 0.4115 -0.0420 0.0426
3 LAIe Lägeren · broadleaf forest temperate_broadleaf_forest 62991 1.7243 2.0045 0.2802 0.2802
4 LAIe Saguaro · arid shrubland arid_shrubland 63001 0.0182 0.0487 0.0305 0.0319
5 LAIe Konza prairie · grassland temperate_nonforest 63001 1.3502 1.1504 -0.1998 0.2000

Interpret differences as sensitivity to model choice. They do not establish which model is more accurate. Both models receive the same local input data; no water or vegetation-class mask is added here. The comparison uses mean retrievals; variant uncertainty currently inherits the global recalibration table.
